title: SOC 2 CC6.1 - Logical Access Security
content: The entity implements logical access security software, infrastructure, and architectures over protected information assets to protect them from security events to meet the entity's objectives.
remediation: Implement strict logical access controls. Enforce Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all system users, and restrict administrative privileges to authorized personnel only.

title: SOC 2 CC6.2 - User Registration and Authorization
content: Prior to issuing system credentials and granting system access, the entity registers and authorizes new internal and external users whose access is administered by the entity.
remediation: Establish a formal user provisioning process. Ensure all access requests are approved by management before granting access, and remove access immediately upon termination.

title: SOC 2 CC6.3 - Access Authorization and Modification
content: The entity authorizes, modifies, or removes access to data, software, functions, and other IT resources based on roles, responsibilities, or the system design and changes, giving consideration to the concepts of least privilege and segregation of duties.
remediation: Enforce the principle of least privilege. Conduct quarterly access reviews to ensure active users only have permissions required for their current roles.

title: PCI DSS Requirement 7 - Restrict Access by Business Need
content: Restrict access to system components and cardholder data by business need to know. Systems and processes must be in place to limit access based on users' job responsibilities.
remediation: Configure access control systems to default to 'deny-all'. Explicitly grant access only when required by a user's job function.

title: PCI DSS Requirement 8 - Identify and Authenticate Users
content: Identify and authenticate access to system components. Assign a unique identification (ID) to each person with computer access to ensure actions taken on critical data and systems are tracked to known and authorized users.
remediation: Disable shared, group, or generic accounts. Ensure every user has a unique ID and enforce MFA for all administrative access into the cardholder data environment.

title: GDPR Article 32 - Security of Processing
content: Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk, including pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data, and the ability to ensure the ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems.
remediation: Audit IAM policies to ensure personal data access is heavily restricted. Implement encryption for data at rest and in transit, and enforce strict least privilege on databases containing PII.

title: HIPAA 164.312(a)(1) - Access Control
content: Implement technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain electronic protected health information (ePHI) to allow access only to those persons or software programs that have been granted access rights.
remediation: Assign unique names/numbers for tracking user identity. Implement automatic logoff procedures and encrypt ePHI to prevent unauthorized access in case of a breach.

title: DPDP Act Section 8(5) - Security Safeguards
content: A Data Fiduciary shall protect personal data in its possession or under its control by taking reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach.
remediation: Implement strict IAM controls, enable audit logging (CloudTrail), and actively monitor for unauthorized or anomalous access to personal data repositories.

title: ISO 27001 Annex A.9.2.1 - User Registration and De-registration
content: A formal user registration and de-registration process shall be implemented to enable assignment of access rights.
remediation: Automate user de-provisioning upon employee offboarding. Ensure access is revoked immediately and conduct periodic audits of active accounts.

title: ISO 27001 Annex A.9.2.3 - Management of Privileged Access Rights
content: The allocation and use of privileged access rights shall be restricted and controlled.
remediation: Identify all privileged accounts and implement Just-In-Time (JIT) access or a Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution to secure elevated permissions.

title: CIS AWS Foundations 1.14 - Restrict IAM Policies
content: Ensure IAM policies are attached only to groups or roles, and not directly to users.
remediation: Detach all inline and managed policies attached directly to IAM users. Assign users to IAM Groups and attach policies to the groups instead to simplify access management and prevent permission sprawl.

title: CIS GCP Foundations 1.1 - Ensure Corporate Login Credentials
content: Ensure that corporate login credentials are used instead of personal accounts (e.g., Gmail accounts) for IAM.
remediation: Remove all @gmail.com accounts from GCP IAM policies. Enforce the use of Google Workspace or Cloud Identity for all enterprise access.
